subject: Business Models
title: The Innovator's Dilemma
description: A quick win: understand The Innovator's Dilemma.

hook.text: Clayton Christensen showed why great companies fail: they listen to existing customers instead of future ones.

buildup.text: Established companies optimize for current customers who want better versions of today's products.

discovery.text: Disruptors start with worse products for overlooked customers, then improve until they steal the mainstream market.

twist.text: Kodak, Blockbuster, Nokia—each dominated and each was disrupted by initially inferior products they dismissed.

climax.text: The dilemma: serving today's best customers optimally blinds you to tomorrow's disruptive threats.

punchline.text: Listening to your best customers can kill you. The innovator's dilemma is real.

quiz.question: What is the core of the innovator's dilemma?
options: Serving current customers well blinds companies to disruptive threats

details.summary: Clayton Christensen's Innovator's Dilemma explains why successful companies fail when disruptive technologies emerge. Incumbents rationally focus on existing profitable customers while dismissing inferior new technologies that improve rapidly and eventually capture the entire market from below.
details.whyItMatters: The Innovator's Dilemma is the most influential framework for understanding business model failure. It explains why rational management decisions lead to predictably catastrophic outcomes when facing disruptive innovation.
takeaways: Incumbents rationally serve profitable customers and ignore low-end disruptions
Disruptive technologies start inferior but improve until they capture the whole market
Good management practices become traps when the basis of competition shifts

faq.question: What is the core mechanism of the Innovator's Dilemma?
faq.answer: Disruptive products start with lower performance serving a niche or low-end market. Incumbents rationally ignore them because margins are lower and existing customers do not want them. The disruptive product improves over time until it meets mainstream needs at lower cost, capturing the market.

faq.question: How can companies avoid the Innovator's Dilemma?
faq.answer: Create separate business units to pursue disruptive technologies without pressure to serve existing customers. Evaluate new technologies on trajectory of improvement rather than current performance. Build a culture that can cannibalize its own products before competitors do.
